title: MetGenX annotates two previously uncharacterized metabolites in mouse liver
summary: MetGenX, a structure-informed neural-network workflow for generating structures from tandem mass spectra, was applied to untargeted mouse-liver metabolomics and reported two previously uncharacterized metabolites, adenosyl-cysteine and adenosine 5′-diphosphate 5′-inosine (Ap2I). The paper reports validation against chemical standards using retention time and MS2 spectral matches.
ai_technology: MetGenX structure-informed encoder-decoder neural network with LightGBM reranking
organization: Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and collaborators

evidence.tested: MetGenX, a structure-informed neural-network workflow for generating structures from tandem mass spectra, was applied to untargeted mouse-liver metabolomics and reported two previously uncharacterized metabolites, adenosyl-cysteine and adenosine 5′-diphosphate 5′-inosine (Ap2I).
evidence.unknown: The original Nature full-text route was inaccessible in this session; the primary-source PubMed article page provides the paper abstract and figure captions describing standard-based retention-time/MS2 matches for the two structures. The finding is metabolite annotation in mouse tissue, not evidence of human biological function. Independent replication was not checked.
evidence.ai_role: The model generated and reranked candidate molecular structures from MS2 spectra; researchers applied a multi-step workflow to mouse-liver samples and compared the two reported metabolite candidates with standards. AI proposed annotations, while standard-based chromatographic and spectral matching supported the assignments.
